subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this `gateway.peers` session-tool routing shape as the cross-gateway contract, or should implementation wait for a broader federation/bridge design?
rationale: This choice changes gateway trust boundaries, session routing authority, configured secret use, replay/idempotency behavior, and message delivery semantics, so automation cannot safely choose it from the PR alone.

options.title: Design the federation contract first
options.body: Keep the PR as context but pause merge until maintainers define peer identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-history ownership; this is the recommended path.

options.title: Narrow and sponsor gateway.peers
options.body: Accept `gateway.peers` as an operator-only feature shape, then require the author or a maintainer to fix protocol/auth bugs, rebase conflicts, and provide real multi-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Close or redirect the PR after documenting the supported external bridge/plugin workaround and keeping the broader federation tracker open.

recommendation.title: Design the federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR as context but pause merge until maintainers define peer identity, scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-history ownership; this is the recommended path.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across gateway protocol/client boundaries and session spawn/send behavior touched by this PR.
